candidates.title: Byte-identical 73-line fixture block (`make_config` / `make_output_context` / `make_system`) copy-pasted between two sibling inline test modules in `output/`

evidence.command: git show a136840d4f2ea137f685f0af6dac04254b983b60:crates/cobre-io/src/output/convergence_reader.rs | sed -n '278,320p' | md5sum; git show a136840d4f2ea137f685f0af6dac04254b983b60:crates/cobre-io/src/output/results_writer.rs | sed -n '276,318p' | md5sum; diff <(sed -n '321,344p' crates/cobre-io/src/output/convergence_reader.rs) <(sed -n '331,354p' crates/cobre-io/src/output/results_writer.rs)
evidence.reading: The two `make_config()` bodies (43 lines each) hash identically at the pinned baseline, so they are byte-for-byte the same fixture. The two 24-line `make_output_context()` bodies differ on exactly one line, and only in how the same `DistributionInfo` type is spelled in a local `use`. `make_system()` (6 lines) is likewise identical. Total duplicated fixture surface between two files in the same directory is roughly 73 lines.

candidates.fixShape: Hoist the three fixtures to a single owner shared by the `output/` inline test modules and have both files call it. The natural home is a `#[cfg(test)]` fixture module under `output/` (a sibling `output/test_fixtures.rs` declared once from `output/mod.rs`, following the `validation/semantic/test_support.rs` precedent already established in this crate), or, if the fixtures are wanted by the crate's integration binaries too, a `test-support`-gated surface on cobre-io mirroring the `test-support` feature cobre-core already exposes. Keep the small value differences the two call sites actually need as arguments rather than forking the body again. Do not merge the two test modules themselves; only the fixture construction moves.

candidates.title: `output/policy/mod.rs` is a 29-line re-export shim carrying a 1315-line inline test module whose 36 tests target the three submodules, which themselves are nearly untested

evidence.command: grep -n '#\[cfg(test)\]' crates/cobre-io/src/output/policy/mod.rs; wc -l crates/cobre-io/src/output/policy/*.rs; for f in codec checkpoint records; do printf '%-12s #[test]=%s\n' "$f" "$(grep -c '#\[test\]' crates/cobre-io/src/output/policy/$f.rs)"; done
evidence.reading: The production body of `policy/mod.rs` ends at line 28 (module doc, three `pub mod` lines, four `pub use` blocks); the `#[cfg(test)]` attribute is at line 30 and the module body runs to line 1344, so 1315 of 1344 lines are test. A classifier over the 37 parsed `#[test]` bodies (matching calls to `serialize_*`/`deserialize_*` versus `write_policy_checkpoint`/`read_policy_checkpoint`) reports 21 codec-only, 15 checkpoint-only, 0 mixed, 1 neither. Meanwhile `codec.rs` (1467 lines) carries 1 inline test and `checkpoint.rs` (317 lines) carries none. The tests are homed two module levels away from the code they exercise, in the one file in the directory with no production logic.

candidates.fixShape: Move each test to the submodule it exercises: the 21 serialize/deserialize tests become an extracted sibling `codec` test module, the 15 write/read-checkpoint tests become a `checkpoint` test module, and the shared record fixtures (`make_cut_record`, `chain_manifest`, `make_metadata`, `make_stage_cuts_payload`, `make_basis_record`, `sample_manifest`) go to one fixture module both import. Leave in `policy/mod.rs` only tests that genuinely assert the composed round trip across all three submodules, if any survive that classification. Apply the yardstick's single homing rule at the same time: above the extraction threshold the module goes to a sibling file, so this lands as `codec/tests.rs` and `checkpoint/tests.rs` rather than as three more giant inline modules. This is a pure relocation, so the migration invariant is unchanged test-function count.

evidence.reading: `all_schema_functions_return_valid_schemas` (line 1282) holds a twenty-row `expected: &[(&str, usize)]` table asserting the field count of every output schema. Fourteen of those counts are asserted a second time by a dedicated per-schema test with the identical literal. Seven of those fourteen are count-only tests whose whole body is that one assertion (`thermals_schema_field_count` and its six siblings at lines 852-1160), so they add no assertion the umbrella does not already make. Adding a column therefore requires two coordinated magic-number edits and produces two failures naming one cause. `transit_seed_schema_field_count` is the one count-only test not in the umbrella table.

candidates.fixShape: Pick one registry for field counts. The umbrella table is the better owner because it is exhaustive and a new schema cannot be added without appearing there, so the seven count-only per-schema tests collapse into it, and `transit_seed` gains the umbrella row it is currently missing. Where a per-schema test also pins the full column-name vector, drop only its redundant length assertion — the name vector already implies the count and, unlike the count, actually pins the output wire contract against a rename. The end state is one count per schema in one table plus name-vector pins per schema, with no number maintained in two places.

evidence.reading: `every_listed_schema_column_has_a_nonempty_description` iterates `variables_csv_schemas()` and asserts `!description_for(file, field).is_empty()` for every column of every listed schema. `variables_csv_schemas()` lists `("hydros", hydros_schema())` and `("hydro_bus_generation", hydro_bus_generation_schema())`, so the two per-schema description tests at lines 3226 and 3239 iterate a subset of the same pairs with the same assertion. All five columns checked by `new_energy_columns_have_descriptions` are declared in `hydros_schema()`, so that test is a five-element subset of the same sweep. None of the three can fail while the exhaustive test passes. `bounds_hydro_id_column_has_a_description` at line 3168 is NOT subsumed — `"bounds"` is absent from `variables_csv_schemas()` — and must be kept.

candidates.fixShape: Delete the three subsumed tests and rely on the exhaustive sweep, which is the stronger gate because a new column added to any listed schema fails it automatically while a per-schema test has to be remembered and written. Keep `bounds_hydro_id_column_has_a_description` and `new_energy_columns_have_units`: the first covers a table the sweep does not list, and the second asserts specific unit strings rather than mere non-emptiness, which is a different property. If the intent behind the three was to pin those particular columns by name rather than to re-check non-emptiness, convert them into the unit-style assertion instead of deleting, so the pin survives and the redundancy does not.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-io/src/output/manifest.rs:571 (`make_training_metadata`) and :635 (`make_simulation_metadata`)
positives.why: The metadata test module uses one fixture builder per type and reaches every variant through functional-update syntax at seven call sites (`..make_training_metadata()` at :864, :895, :977, :1062, :1091; `..make_simulation_metadata()` at :730, :760), so adding a field to `TrainingMetadata` costs one edit rather than seven. This is the O(1) fixture field-add pattern the yardstick names as a strength, already practised inside sub-station D — it is the model the two duplicated-fixture candidates above should be aligned to, not an instance of the problem.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-io/tests/metadata_back_compat.rs:1-24 and its `legacy_*_fixture_omits_new_keys` tests (:167, :191)
positives.why: The legacy fixtures are hand-frozen JSON literals with the reason recorded in the file header — a struct-serialized fixture carries every field and so could never catch a field accidentally made required — and two further tests guard the fixtures themselves against acquiring the new keys. A self-guarding fixture whose deliberate non-reuse is justified in place; the test-bloat lens must not propose folding these into a shared builder.
positives.sanctionedBy: docs/design/testing-architecture.md §3.1 item 2 (contract-pinning) — the fixture is the pin, and the `*_omits_new_keys` tests are its power self-check

positives.subject: crates/cobre-core/src/entities/hydro.rs::declare_mirror_unit_group (line 277, behind `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]`)
positives.why: The cross-crate sharing mechanism the yardstick prescribes exists and is genuinely consumed from sub-station D: cobre-io declares the dev-dependency with the feature on (crates/cobre-io/Cargo.toml:44) and calls the symbol from `output/simulation_writer.rs:2095` and `output/dictionary.rs:1445`, among roughly a hundred workspace call sites. The seam is proven and available — it is the landing zone the fixture-consolidation candidates should extend, not a mechanism that needs inventing.

_needsHuman: Whether the double-pinned field counts in `schemas.rs` are deliberate belt-and-braces for a published output wire contract or accidental drift; if deliberate, the owner should say which of the two sites is the intended registry so the other can be reduced rather than both kept.

Whether `output/policy/mod.rs` hosts the codec and checkpoint tests deliberately, because they are meant to exercise only the crate-public re-export surface, or incidentally; the 21 codec-only tests reach `serialize_*`/`deserialize_*` through `use super::*` and would resolve equally well beside `codec.rs`, but a deliberate re-export-surface intent would change the fix shape from relocation to leaving them in place.

Whether cobre-io should gain its own `test-support` feature to share output fixtures with its twelve integration binaries, or whether an internal `#[cfg(test)]` fixture module under `output/` is sufficient; the answer decides the landing zone for both fixture-duplication candidates and is a crate-surface decision beyond this sub-station.
